subject: Astrapay onboarding: traffic sweep schedule and benchmark results
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@astrapay.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@astrapay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-10T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed traffic sweep plan and acceptance targets

Hi Alex / Priya —

As discussed on the onboarding call, we want to run a set of controlled traffic sweeps so we can validate the integration and generate the benchmark artifacts you need for internal sign-off. Attached is a short CSV with the proposed windows and payload mixes (astrapay-traffic-sweep-plan.csv).

High-level targets we propose for acceptance testing (initial):
- p50 token latency: <= 80ms
- p95 token latency: <= 200ms
- p99 token latency: <= 300ms
- Sustained throughput target: 120 requests/sec (with 4 concurrent clients)
- Error rate threshold: < 0.5%

Planned sweeps:
1) Ramp test (10 -> target over 10m)
2) Sustained run (60m at target)
3) Spike test (short bursts to 2x target)

Questions for you: please confirm an execution window (we were thinking Tue 16 Feb 14:00–16:00 PST), and let us know if you have a preferred payload distribution (short chat prompts vs. long form) — default plan uses 70/30 short/long.

We will run on the rwd-gpt-7b-q4 model variant and will capture token-level latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and KV cache hit rates. I’ve CC’d Karthik to coordinate infra checks.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Implementation Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: astrapay-traffic-sweep-plan.csv (stub)
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@astrapay.com>

Date: 2026-02-11T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed traffic sweep plan and acceptance targets

Thanks Ben — the plan looks good. Tue 16 Feb 14:00–16:00 PST works for us.

A couple of clarifications:
- Payloads: we’ll provide two sample sets this afternoon — one short (avg 50 tokens) and one long (avg 420 tokens).
- We typically run client-side concurrency of 6 by default; are you recommending 4? If so we can adjust the client harness.
- Will Redwood run with a cache warmer ahead of the sustained run, or do you want cold-start numbers too?

We’ll push a small terraform change to the test cluster later today to increase API worker counts in case we need headroom.

—Alex
Alex Jenkins
Head of Engineering, Astrapay

> (original plan attached)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@astrapay.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@astrapay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-12T08:26:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed traffic sweep plan and acceptance targets

Alex — thanks, good questions. Quick clarifications and the exact test recipe below.

1) Concurrency: we’ll run the main sustained test with 4 load clients hitting the Redwood stack to match the throughput profile we designed. If you prefer 6 client-side concurrency we can exercise that as a separate sweep — it changes client connection profiles but not target TPS.

2) Cache warming: we suggest collecting both cold-start (first 5m) and warmed metrics. For the signed-off acceptance we typically evaluate the warmed steady-state numbers — we’ll run a 10-minute warm-up before the sustained window and capture cold-start in an earlier sweep.

3) Test recipe (what Redwood will run):
- Model: rwd-gpt-7b-q4 (float emulation path)
- Sequence lengths: short=50 tokens, long=420 tokens
- Batching config: adaptive batching with max_batch_size=32, max_latency_ms=12
- Sweeps: ramp (10m), warm-up (10m), sustained (60m), spike (3 x 2m bursts at 2x)
- Metrics: token-level p50/p95/p99, end-to-end request latency, token/s, GPU util, batch sizes, KV cache hit rate, error count by type

We’ll push a sample log snippet to the shared drive after the first run (log-sample-0216.txt). If the p99 is trending above 300ms we’ll pair with your infra to test prefix caching and a higher batch ceiling.

Ben

Attachments: None
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@astrapay.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Pre-checks: infra health and harness readiness

Morning team — quick pre-sweep note. I ran the infra pre-check script against the Astrapay test endpoint this morning (connectivity, TLS, concurrency smoke). Observations:
- Greenwood autoscaler config on Astrapay side had a min_replicas=1 which caused slow ramp behavior; I see you pushed a fix (thanks).
- Redwood agents and load harness are green from our side. We put a temporary cap on max_batch_size=24 to reduce tail latency for the first run; we can relax after seeing results.
- Small heads-up: client-side concurrency set to 6 pushed 20% higher socket churn — recommend we start with 4 for the sustained window then iterate.

I’ve uploaded a short pre-check snapshot to the drive and linked the dashboard below.

Dashboard: https://redwood.example.com/drive/astrapay/benchmarks (telemetry view)

Karthik
Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@astrapay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-16T15:32:00-08:00
Subject: Initial benchmark upload + questions

Hi all — thanks for running the sweep. I’ve attached the first-pass PDF summary (20260216-benchmark-summary.pdf). Quick notes from our side:
- Sustained 60m run: p50=72ms, p95=190ms, p99=330ms (token-level). We missed the p99 target by ~30ms.
- Error rate was 0.2% (within threshold). GPU utilization averaged 68%.

Questions / suggestions:
1) Is the 330ms p99 coming from batching/backpressure or from occasional cold KV lookups?
2) We can enable prefix caching on our side if that helps; what's the expected p99 improvement?

Attached artifacts: 20260216-benchmark-summary.pdf (stub). I also included a small log excerpt.

—Alex

Attachments: 20260216-benchmark-summary.pdf, log-sample-0216.txt
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@astrapay.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@astrapay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-17T16:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial benchmark upload + questions — next steps and acceptance criteria

Thanks Alex and team — good data and appreciate the quick turnaround. A short summary and proposed actions:

Summary:
- Sustained run p99=330ms (missed by ~30ms vs our initial target). Other metrics look healthy.
- Error rate and GPU profile are within expectations — no infra faults observed from the Redwood side.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Enable prefix caching on Astrapay for the sustained run; we expect this to reduce KV lookup tail events and should bring p99 down by ~20–40ms based on similar workloads.
2) Relax Redwood batch cap to max_batch_size=32 for the next test to see if batching improves throughput without increasing tail.
3) Re-run the sustained 60m sweep on Fri 19 Feb 09:00–11:00 PST (please confirm).

Acceptance ask for final signoff: if warmed sustained p99 <= 300ms and error rate < 0.5% we will mark the onboarding benchmark as satisfied for the performance gate. If we still miss by a narrow margin, we’ll document mitigations and recommend a production rollout cadence with a staged traffic ramp.

Action items assigned:
- Astrapay: enable prefix caching and confirm by EOD Thu (Alex)
- Redwood infra: revert batch cap and provide new run artifacts (Karthik/Ben)
- CS: collect signoff once final artifact is posted (Monica)

I’ll push the run artifacts to the shared drive and the HubSpot deal record with the note (deal DL-2026-089). Thanks everyone — we’ll be on call during the Friday sweep.

Ben
Implementation Manager, Redwood Inference
